facts.statement: Australornis is considered one of the oldest known flying seabirds.
facts.quote: Australornis is one of the oldest flying seabirds.

facts.statement: It was the first fossil of a non-penguin seabird discovered in New Zealand from the Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: It is also the first non-sphenisciform (penguins and allies) bird fossil discovered from New Zealand for that age.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 2009 by amateur paleontologist Leigh Love in north Canterbury, New Zealand.
facts.quote: The fossil was discovered in 2009 by Leigh Love in the Paleocene Waipara Greensand of north Canterbury on the South Island of New Zealand.

facts.statement: Australornis lived during the Paleocene epoch, between 60.5 and 61.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived in the Paleocene epoch, 60.5 to 61.6 million years ago (Ma).

facts.statement: Australornis grew to a length of roughly 70 to 85 cm, similar in size to a pied shag.
facts.quote: Australornis grew roughly to about 70 to 85 cm long, and has been likened to a pied shag in size.

facts.statement: It is estimated that Australornis weighed between 1.5 and 2 kg.
facts.quote: It is thought to have weighed between 1.5 to 2 kg.

facts.statement: The fossil record includes right coracoid, scapula, humerus, ulna, radius fragments, and a left carpal bone.
facts.quote: Australornis is known from the following remains: right coracoid (extremitas omalis) right scapula (caudal portion) right humerus (less the distal end) right ulna (proximal end only) fragments of the shaft of a radius left os carpi radiale

facts.statement: A 2017 study classified Australornis as a stem-anseriform within the family Vegaviidae.
facts.quote: In 2017 a phylogenetic study Agnolín and colleagues have found Australornis to be stem-anseriforms along with Polarornis, Neogaeornis and Vegavis in the family Vegaviidae.

facts.statement: Although found near the oldest known penguin fossils, Australornis lacks any morphological resemblance to penguins.
facts.quote: Though Australornis was found near the fossils of Waimanu manneringi, the oldest fossil penguin, found in the same level of strata in Waipara and regarded to be of the same age, it lacks any morphological resemblances to penguins.

facts.statement: Australornis is classified within the family Vegaviidae.
The genus Australornis was named by G. Mayr and R.P. Scofield in 2014.
The type species Australornis lovei was named by G. Mayr and R.P. Scofield in 2014.
The time range for the genus Australornis is estimated from 61.66 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the fossil evidence is sufficient to fully substantiate phylogeny, though it supports the view that Neoaves diversification began in the earliest Paleogene.
facts.quote: Though the fossil evidence is incomplete to substantiate phylogeny, Australornis contributes to the emerging view that the diversification of Neoaves had already begun in the earliest Paleogene.
